newsitem.title: UK: Copper price at five-month high, stocks drop.
newsitem.headline: Copper price at five-month high, stocks drop.

text.p: Copper prices raced to their highest for five months above $2,200 per tonne on Tuesday on news of falling world stocks.
Data showed a fresh decline of 5,050 tonnes in stocks held in warehouses supervised by the London Metal Exchange (LME).
The drop took them to their lowest in six years and below the important psychological threshold of 100,000 tonnes.
In reaction LME three months delivery copper chased to a high at $2,232 a tonne, up on Monday's LME close of $2,159.
"The stocks fall has come as a boost to copper after it broke above key resistance at $2,200 a tonne on Monday," one trader said.
Others agreed and believed copper, after a period of consolidation, had the potential to move towards next technical resistance at $2,275/78.
Suggestions last week that big off-market stocks of copper might have been hoarded in Europe appeared to have been greeted with scepticism in the market.
"We are eyeing visible warranted LME stocks which continue to fall...that is our yardstick," an LME floor trader said.

Copper prices have been extremely volatile since June when Japan's Sumitomo Corp sacked its star trader, Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging that he ran up losses on maverick deals in copper worth $2.6 billion. Hamanaka was the architect of a high price trading strategy and was believed by traders to have hoarded stocks to support a copper price that, in May, ran up as high at $2,715.
It fell soon after his disgrace as low at $1,745 as fears that Sumitomo was unwinding his huge long position unnerved the market.
The latest rally means that copper has now recouped almost half the post-Hamanaka loss.
